correctness.rationale: Every lower source chooses a lower target, independently of all upper sources; an upper b-block has d=b! bijective maps to each large target and w_B=|B|!S(b,|B|) surjections to a lower B, giving the multinomial probabilities. Marked Bernoulli-to-Poisson coupling and a Poisson increment bound total variation by 2C²/(Md²). Sarkar–Singh’s regularity criterion follows from the existence of an equal-size source for each image target. The upper size class is automatically witnessed; for a lower target B hit by upper sources, regularity requires a lower equal-size source. This yields the exact conditional avoidance factor and R_M. Conditioning the limiting Poisson vector gives forced zeros in missing-witness coordinates, unchanged independent Poisson coordinates elsewhere, and tilt exp(−Σ_missing w/d). The bound 4C²/(Md²R∞) follows from elementary conditioning. Fresh independent complete finite map enumeration for three mixed block patterns matched exact regular counts; not used as proof of convergence.

value.rationale: The conditional law captures which lower blocks are hit by many large source blocks and explains the asymptotic population of regular elements in a natural transformation semigroup. It distinguishes random unconditioned surjections from those satisfying a semigroup-theoretic generalized inverse, providing a usable finite-background limit law and rates.

final_claim: A uniform block-surjective map on fixed smaller blocks plus M labelled largest blocks has an exact independent multinomial rare-lower-target vector, joint Poisson limit with explicit O(1/M) total-variation rate, and an explicit conditional tilted-Poisson law given von Neumann regularity.
limitations: Explicit TV bound can be vacuous for small M; no claims when b or the background grow with M.
